title: Serialized window shard mismatch causing cross-service throttling and customer outages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-12 we observed a surge of opaque 429s across multiple tenants in Hosted and Dedicated. Investigation shows a mismatch in how rate-window state was serialized and sharded between the edge proxy layer and the quota orchestrator. The mismatch caused window epochs to diverge during a partial orchestrator upgrade, leading to large numbers of requests evaluated against an expired/sharded window and resulting in premature throttles. Several high-volume customers opened escalations reporting persistent throttling for 10–45 minutes. This ticket documents investigation, mitigations, root cause, and long-term remediation plan.
impact: Multiple high-volume tenants experienced sustained request failures (429) for 10–45 minutes during peak traffic. A subset of Dedicated customers reported SLA violations and elevated support escalations. Estimated revenue impact: medium (customers on dedicated committed capacity were rate-limited unexpectedly). Operational overhead: pager rotations and manual rollbacks on two clusters.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy orchestrator with mixed version (old/new) while edge proxies have continuous per-tenant window serialization format A.
2) Send traffic with burst patterns (hundreds of QPS per tenant) and observe quota ledger entries created on both versions.
3) Trigger a reconciliation flow (orchestrator leader handoff) that forces partial replay/merge of shard state.
4) Observe divergence: proxies evaluate token bucket using epoch X while orchestrator believes epoch X+1 and rejects requests as exhausted.
observed_signals_and_logs:
- Spike in 429 rate across regions starting 2026-03-12T01:17Z.
- Orchestrator leader handoff logs show 'applied-epoch: 37412' and proxies report 'window-epoch: 37411' for same tenant.
- Quota ledger snapshots indicate missing epoch delta reconciliations for sharded keys.
- Support tickets and escalations: #TICKET-2345, #TICKET-2346 from major customers.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 (rollback performed).
root_cause_summary: During a rolling upgrade to introduce compact serialization for window shards, we introduced a version negotiation bug: the orchestrator accepted compact shards and wrote a newer epoch semantics into the centralized ledger, but the edge proxy deserializer fell back to legacy interpretation for shards with a particular flag. This produced asymmetric epoch advancement across services. The reconciliation logic incorrectly assumed idempotence across formats and skipped epoch-gap correction when encountering the legacy flag, resulting in stale window state being evaluated as current and causing premature quota exhaustion.
mitigations_applied:
1) Emergency rollback of orchestrator change to previous serialization format in affected clusters (completed 2026-03-12T02:05Z).
2) Short-lived global bypass: edge proxies temporarily accepted both formats and bypassed strict epoch checks for 5 minutes during reconciliation window.
3) Replayed ledger snapshots to correct epoch counters for tenants that saw divergence.
4) Customer comms: sent incident bulletin to affected customers and opened dedicated support threads.
5) Added a temporary monitoring rule to alert on epoch drift > 0 for a tenant for more than 2 minutes.
long_term_fix:
1) Implement compatible forward/backward schema for window shards with explicit version headers and a robust negotiation handshake.
2) Harden reconciliation logic: do not skip epoch-gap correction when encountering unknown flags; instead, surface to orchestrator and perform deterministic merge.
3) Add end-to-end integration tests (proxy+orchestrator+reconciliation) that exercise mixed-format rolling upgrades.
4) Add unit tests around serialization/epoch semantics and fuzz tests for shard boundaries.
5) Plan phased rollout with feature gate and canary traffic at 1% with automated rollback on epoch-drift alerts.
testing_plan:
- Local integration matrix: proxy v1/v2 x orchestrator v1/v2 with simulated traffic patterns and leader handoffs.
- Staging canary: deploy changes to staging cluster, enable feature gate for a small set of tenants, run load generator mimicking customer burst profiles.
- Blue-green controlled rollouts in prod with traffic ramp and epoch-drift gating; require zero occurrences of drift > 1 minute before expanding.
- Post-deploy regression: run nightly chaos test that simulates leader failovers and sharded ledger merges.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Merge and run full integration tests (2 days).
Phase 1: Canary (1% tenants) with feature gate and automatic rollback on alert (3 days).
Phase 2: Progressive rollout to remaining clusters with monitoring escalations (5 days).
Contingency: Immediate rollback to legacy serialization in any cluster with drift or customer reports.
timeline: 2026-03-12 01:10Z - first alerts; 01:22Z - identified orchestrator serialization change as suspect; 01:50Z - emergency rollback initiated; 02:05Z - rollback completed; 02:30Z - ledger replay and corrections finished; 03:00Z - alerts subsided. Postmortem drafting started same day.
decision_notes: We elected to roll back rather than attempt in-place conversion because the rollback path had a lower risk envelope and allowed deterministic ledger correction. The long-term plan is to add explicit schema versions and reconcile on epoch gaps rather than skipping. Product concurs that this must be prioritized before the next runtime release.
